record.original_question: Describe the cycle structure of Costas permutations under iteration. In particular, for a specific Costas permutation or a specific family, determine the full cycle decomposition, whether cycles of a given length can occur, the longest cycle length, and the smallest positive integer k for which the k-fold iterate equals the identity permutation.

evidence.quote: Definition 9. Let f : [n] → [n] be a permutation, and let I : [n] → [n] be the identity: I(i) = i. Let f (0) = I, and, for any k ∈ N, let f (k+1) = f(f (k)), in the sense that, for any i ∈ [n], f (k+1)(i) = f(f (k)(i)). The cycle of i under f is the set {f (k)(i) : k ∈ N}, which is necessarily finite, containing at most n elements.

Problem 9. Describe the cycle structure of Costas permutations. In particular, • Determine the cycle structure of a particular Costas permutation; • Determine the existence/absence of cycles of a particular length in a specific Costas permutation, or a family thereof; • Determine the longest cycle in a specific Costas permutation, or a family thereof; • Determine the smallest k for which f (k) = I for a specific Costas permutation f, or a family thereof.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A Costas array of order n is an n×n array with exactly one dot in each row and each column such that all (n choose 2) displacement vectors between pairs of distinct dots are distinct. Equivalently, a Costas permutation of order n is a bijection f : [n] → [n] (where [n] = {1, 2, …, n}) whose graph is a Costas array; that is, for every choice of integers i, j, k with 1 ≤ i < i+k ≤ n and 1 ≤ j < j+k ≤ n with (i, j) ≠ (i+k, j+k) lying in [n], the equation f(i+k) − f(i) = f(j+k) − f(j) implies (i, j) = (i+k, j+k); equivalently, the differences f(i+k) − f(i) are distinct for each fixed k ∈ {1, …, n−1} as i varies.

Let I : [n] → [n] denote the identity permutation, and define iterates of f by f^(0) = I and f^(k+1)(i) = f(f^(k)(i)) for all i ∈ [n] and k ∈ ℕ. The cycle of i ∈ [n] under f is the (finite) set {f^(k)(i) : k ∈ ℕ}.

Investigate the cycle structure of Costas permutations under iteration. In particular, address the following:

(a) For specified Costas permutations or specified families of Costas permutations (for instance, the Welch and Lempel–Golomb families arising from primitive roots of finite fields), determine the full cycle decomposition.

(b) Determine, for such a permutation or family, which cycle lengths can occur and which are forbidden.

(c) Determine the longest cycle length appearing in such a permutation or family.

(d) Determine the order of f, that is, the smallest positive integer k such that f^(k) = I.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of describing the cycle structure of Costas permutations under iteration is listed as one of the open problems in the literature on Costas arrays. Some partial results exist for specific algebraic families (e.g., Welch and Golomb/Lempel constructions), but no general description of cycle decomposition, longest cycle length, or order of Costas permutations is known.

status_evidence.title: Open problems in Costas arrays
status_evidence.snippet: A collection of open problems in Costas arrays is presented, including the problem of describing the cycle structure of Costas permutations.
status_evidence.claim: The cycle structure of Costas permutations is listed among open problems in the area.

status_evidence.title: On the degrees of freedom of Costas permutations and other constraints
status_evidence.snippet: Studies constraints on Golomb Costas permutations, including iterated compositions producing Lempel Costas permutations in suitable subfields.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial results connecting iterated compositions of certain Golomb Costas permutations to other Costas permutations are known.
